questions.q: What is the recommended fastest path for running MongoDB locally for this course, per this lesson?
options: Running MongoDB's official Docker image, e.g. `docker run -d --name mongodb -p 27017:27017 mongo:latest`
There is no way to run MongoDB locally — it requires a cloud account
Compiling MongoDB from source is the only supported option
MongoDB can only run inside a Neo4j container
questions.explain: The official Docker image is called out as the fastest, most isolated, most disposable option for this course.

questions.q: What do ports 7474 and 7687 correspond to when running Neo4j via Docker?
options: 7474 is the Neo4j Browser web interface; 7687 is the Bolt protocol used by drivers and cypher-shell
Both ports serve the exact same purpose as a redundancy measure
7474 is for backups and 7687 is for authentication only
These ports are used exclusively by MongoDB, not Neo4j
questions.explain: 7474 serves the browser-based Neo4j Browser UI, while 7687 is the Bolt protocol port drivers and cypher-shell use to connect.

questions.q: Why does the NEO4J_AUTH environment variable matter when starting the Neo4j Docker container?
options: Neo4j requires credentials to be set on first run rather than defaulting to an open, unauthenticated instance
It sets the Docker container's CPU and memory limits
It has no real effect and can be safely omitted
It configures which port MongoDB listens on
questions.explain: NEO4J_AUTH sets the initial username/password since Neo4j doesn't default to an open instance.

questions.q: What real limitation does the Cosmos DB Emulator have compared to a real Azure free-tier account, per this lesson?
options: It doesn't reproduce multi-region distribution behavior, which matters by the time you reach global distribution topics
It cannot run the Core (SQL) API at all
It requires a paid Azure subscription to install
It only works on Linux, never Windows
questions.explain: The emulator is a great free local option but doesn't reproduce Cosmos DB's real multi-region distribution features, which matter later in the course.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should you verify about your MongoDB setup before moving into Chapter 2?
options: That a mongosh connection to localhost:27017 succeeds
That MongoDB Compass has already been fully configured with dashboards
That a Cosmos DB account has been linked to the MongoDB instance
That the MongoDB instance is running in a multi-region cluster
questions.explain: Confirming the port actually responds via a mongosh connection is the verification step this lesson calls for before moving on.
